data.title: Turn a Linear webhook delivery into a foregent event
data.description:
Add `linear.webhook_event(payload) -> Event | None`: a pure mapping from a Linear webhook body to foregent's own event shape. Write it against the payloads `/webhooks/linear` has been logging since JIM-128, not against a guess at the schema.

## Scope

* Any payload naming an issue foregent could be tracking maps. `Comment` becomes `EventKind.COMMENT` with the comment text as the body; everything else that carries an issue (`Issue` create/update/remove, reactions, labels, attachments) becomes a new `EventKind.ISSUE_UPDATE`.
* The issue key comes from `data.issue.identifier` or `data.identifier`. A payload with no issue identifier returns `None`, and so does one whose shape the mapper does not recognize — an unknown payload is dropped, never guessed at.
* Fill in the actor id from the payload. `wakes()` drops foregent's own writes by actor identity, and this path now carries the writes agents make through the Linear MCP *and* the assignee/state change foregent makes when it claims an issue. A mapping that loses the actor turns every claim into a self-wake loop.
* For `ISSUE_UPDATE`, build the body from `updatedFrom` — the changed fields with their previous values (`state: Todo → Cancelled`) — so a worker can act on the update without re-reading the issue.
* `events.py` currently says a Linear field update is deliberately not a wake. That decision reverses here; update the module docstring and `docs/PLAN.md` §5.1 with it.

Mapping only. Nothing is delivered and no route changes — that is the next ticket.

## Acceptance

Unit tests over captured payloads: a comment, an issue update with several changed fields, a payload with no issue, one of an unrecognized type, and one written by foregent's own account (which must carry the actor through so the filter can drop it).
